ai.description: Amolops chakrataensis is a small frog (30–35 mm) with a brownish-grey dorsum and mottled flanks. It features a distinct white upper lip stripe and expanded, truncate toe discs for clinging to rocks.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Amolops chakrataensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous dorsolateral fold that extends from behind the eye to the groin.
ai.habitat: *Amolops chakrataensis* inhabits fast-flowing, rocky mountain streams within moist temperate forests at elevations ranging from 1,800 to 2,200 meters in the Himalayas.
ai.behavior: The Dehradun stream frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining active along rocky mountain streams where it hunts for small invertebrates under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Amolops chakrataensis* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), laying clutches of pigmented eggs attached to submerged rocks in streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Amolops chakrataensis* is endemic to the Chakrata region of Uttarakhand in the Western Himalayas, occurring at elevations between 1,500 and 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Dehradun Stream Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched, pulsed chirps while perched on rocks near fast-flowing mountain streams.
